questions.stem: On a heating curve, the flat sections (where temperature stays constant) represent:

options.text: Periods when no energy is being supplied
Changes of state, where energy breaks bonds between particles
Periods when the substance is cooling down

questions.explanation: The flat sections on a heating curve represent changes of state. During these periods, the energy being supplied is used to break bonds between particles (increasing potential energy) rather than increasing kinetic energy, so the temperature remains constant.

questions.stem: Which factor does NOT increase the rate of evaporation?

options.text: Increasing the temperature of the liquid
Increasing the surface area of the liquid
Increasing the pressure above the liquid
Creating a draught (air flow) over the surface

questions.explanation: Increasing the pressure above the liquid actually decreases the rate of evaporation because it makes it harder for particles to escape from the surface. Higher temperature, larger surface area, and air flow over the surface all increase the evaporation rate.
